title: Conductor app build
subtitle: Repository and workspace management for the Notis cloud computer, built and proven on one user's sandbox.

identifiers.Sandbox tier: ULTRA, 2 vCPU, 4 GB RAM, 21 GB free

acceptance.title: Onboarding works from scratch
acceptance.detail: A user with no configured repository is taken through GitHub sign-in and into their first repository setup.
acceptance.evidence:
Device flow completed from the sandbox: code issued, polled, authenticated as mindtheflo with scopes gist, read:org, repo, workflow. Commit identity set from the GitHub account.
Re-proven through a real conversation: Notis refused the chat-attachment route unprompted and pointed at the app control.

acceptance.title: The notis repository can be set up
acceptance.detail: Cloned under the repositories root, secrets staged, bootstrap scripts resolved, project proven to run.
acceptance.evidence:
Cloned to /vercel/sandbox/repositories/notis (343M, beta).
  discover -> setup=./setup.sh dev=./dev.sh archive=./archive.sh
  prereqs  -> python3.12 installed (image ships 3.9)
  secrets  -> portal/.env, server/.env, website/.env staged outside every checkout
  setup    -> ran detached, exit 0

acceptance.title: A workspace can be created to spec
acceptance.detail: Git worktree from a base branch or pull request, branch named from the task, recorded in the app.
acceptance.evidence:
workspace.sh new notis --task 'add a workspaces smoke note proving the cloud computer flow'
  branch notis/add-a-workspaces-smoke-note-proving-the-cloud-co off beta
  worktree at /vercel/sandbox/workspaces/notis/add-a-workspaces-smoke-note-proving-the-cloud-co
  3 env files applied and excluded from git

acceptance.title: A pull request can be opened
acceptance.detail: Commit and push from inside the worktree, pull request opened with the GitHub CLI.
acceptance.evidence:
Conversation-driven: https://github.com/mindtheflo/notis/pull/1873, OPEN, fix-duplicate-reminder -> beta.
  diff is one file, +3/-0, no .env
  verified with git ls-files and git diff --name-only origin/beta..HEAD

acceptance.title: The app reflects every state
acceptance.detail: Repositories and Workspaces routes show setup state, branch, pull request state and checks.
acceptance.evidence: App deployed (version 2). Live verify passes and a live screenshot of the deployed bundle shows the real state: with every row archived it renders the three-step onboarding, which is what the account actually contains.

acceptance.title: The sandbox agent can run the notis test suite
acceptance.detail: The /notis-tests skill runs inside the workspace on the sandbox.
acceptance.evidence:
Inside the workspace on the sandbox:
  python 3.12.12 venv, portal dependencies installed
  /notis-tests reachable at .claude/skills/notis-tests -> .agents/skills/tools/notis-tests
  server/tests: 6301 passed, 13 failed, 22 skipped in 240s
  12 failures are sandbox-environment dependent, 1 fails identically on origin/beta
This is the non-LLM suite lane. The full branch-validation lane needs a second backend running against production, which was not started.

acceptance.title: Environment files reach the sandbox without being published
acceptance.detail: The app sends the files straight to the cloud computer; nothing is stored by Notis and no URL is minted.
acceptance.evidence:
runtime_query LOCAL_NOTIS_UPLOAD_SANDBOX_FILE -> 200, sha256 matches the source bytes, file on disk at mode 600.
Same surface calling list_sandbox_files and download_sandbox_file -> 403 both times.

findings.title: The GitHub CLI is installed but signed out
findings.detail: gh 2.97.0 is on PATH and .gitconfig already routes GitHub credentials through 'gh auth git-credential', but 'gh auth status' reports no logged-in host and no GH_TOKEN or GITHUB_TOKEN is present in the sandbox environment. Every clone, push and pull request in this feature depends on that credential, so setup could not have worked as assumed.
findings.fix: The repository skill runs the GitHub device flow directly against github.com/login/device/code with the GitHub CLI's own public client id, shows the user the one-time code, polls for the grant, then pipes the token into 'gh auth login --with-token'. That is scriptable without a TTY, which 'gh auth login --web' is not.

findings.title: The sandbox ships Python 3.9 but the notis bootstrap needs 3.12
findings.detail: /usr/bin/python3 is 3.9.25 and there is no python3.12 on PATH, while setup.sh opens with 'python3.12 -m venv server/.venv'. Repository setup would fail on its first line.
findings.fix: The image is Amazon Linux 2023 with passwordless root sudo and python3.12 available in the default repository, so the skill installs the interpreter as a prerequisite step before running the repository's own bootstrap script.

findings.title: Repository setup outlives the per-command timeout
findings.detail: Sandbox commands are capped at twelve minutes. A cold notis setup is a pip install plus six or more npm installs on two vCPUs, which is well past that, so a foreground run is guaranteed to be killed part way through and leave a half-installed tree.
findings.fix: Long steps run detached with nohup against a log file and a status marker, and the skill polls the marker. That also survives the agent's own turn ending.

findings.title: The notis repository has no install.sh
findings.detail: The requested skill contract names install.sh, dev.sh and archive.sh. This repository's bootstrap script is setup.sh; dev.sh and archive.sh do exist. Hard-coding the three names would either fail here or force a rename of a script the whole team uses.
findings.fix: Each repository row stores its own setup, dev and archive commands. The skill discovers an existing bootstrap script and records it; it only writes new scripts when a repository genuinely has none.

findings.title: The executable bit does not survive bundle transport
findings.detail: Scripts arrive in the sandbox without the executable bit, so the first run died with 'Permission denied' when one script called another. The skill instructions already told the agent to use 'bash <path>', but the scripts were calling each other directly.
findings.fix: Every internal script-to-script call names its interpreter. The packaging step still sets the bit for anyone reading the bundle on disk, but nothing depends on it.

findings.title: App-declared skills cannot carry their scripts
findings.detail: notis.config.ts can declare skills from the app source tree, which is the right packaging model, but only the entrypoint's markdown is read. Both of these skills are a few hundred lines of shell and Python and cannot be inlined.
findings.fix: Skills are packaged and published separately, then attached to the app through bundled_skill_ids. Verified: the full bundle including scripts/ materialises under /vercel/sandbox/.notis/skills/<name>/ through the normal sync path.

findings.title: A local dev backend gives the sandbox an unreachable API base
findings.detail: The sandbox received NOTIS_API_BASE=http://localhost:3001 from the local server, so its CLI could not call home and every row write from inside the sandbox failed with a network error.
findings.fix: Sandbox commands in this build pass the user's real service origin explicitly. Recorded in the wishlist: the resolver should not inject a loopback address into a remote sandbox.

findings.title: apps verify refuses to run without Store screenshots
findings.detail: Verify is the render check, but it fails on listing metadata before it renders anything. Scaffolding from notis-database also left that app's five screenshots behind, so the first failure was about alt text for another app's gallery.
findings.fix: Stale scaffold assets removed, four screenshots declared and generated from fixtures. Both routes now verify clean.

findings.title: An absolute path in any row property made every CLI write fail
findings.detail: Writing a row whose text property held an absolute path returned 503 file_target_schema_unavailable. Any value starting with a slash is read as a raw local file reference, which forces a provider file-upload schema lookup; a generated row-write tool has no such schema and never will, so the failure was permanent while the message invited a retry. This app stores checkout and secrets paths, so nothing could be recorded at all. It affects any Notis database holding a path.
findings.fix: The raw-reference heuristic now skips generated row-write tools, which declare no file-uploadable argument. Provider tools still fail closed, so passing a local path as a Dropbox file body is still refused. Extracted as a named predicate with unit tests covering both directions, and verified live: the same write that returned 503 now succeeds.

findings.title: The sandbox image has no /dev/fd, so bash process substitution fails
findings.detail: Every 'while read ... < <(command)' died with '/dev/fd/63: No such file or directory'. /proc/self/fd exists but /dev/fd does not, so the shell cannot open the substituted stream. Any script written on a normal Linux or macOS box will hit this.
findings.fix: The three loops that used process substitution write to a temp file and read from it, which is portable and keeps the loop in the calling shell so its counters survive.

findings.title: Env files copied into a workspace showed up as untracked
findings.detail: Creating a workspace copies the repository's env files into the new tree. For a repository that does not already ignore them, they appear in git status, which is one careless 'git add -A' away from committing a secret. Warning about it in the skill instructions is not a guarantee.
findings.fix: Applying secrets also appends each file to the repository's info/exclude, which is per-checkout and never committed, so it works even for repositories whose .gitignore we do not control. First attempt wrote to the worktree gitdir, where git does not read it; corrected to the common dir. The tree now reports clean with the env file in place.

findings.title: The worktree CLI credential expires after an hour
findings.detail: Mid-build every local CLI call started returning auth_expired for the worktree profile, which reads as missing data: a database query returned zero rows for a database that demonstrably had rows. Sandbox-side calls were unaffected because the sandbox mints its own token per command, so the two surfaces disagreed about the same data.
findings.fix: Restarting the dev session mints a fresh credential. Worth knowing before diagnosing an empty query as a data problem. --refresh-portal-entry-link does not refresh it; only a restart does.

findings.title: Pull request status never appeared, because the lookup used a flag that does not exist
findings.detail: Sync called 'gh pr view --repo <url> --head <branch>'. gh pr view has no --head flag -- that belongs to gh pr list -- so the command failed on every call. The failure was swallowed by 2>/dev/null and reported as 'this workspace has no pull request', which is exactly what a workspace without one looks like. An open pull request stayed invisible in the app.
findings.fix: Sync runs 'gh pr view' from inside the worktree with no selector, which resolves the pull request for the checked-out branch. Verified against a real one: the row now reads Open with its number, URL and check rollup.

findings.title: Staging an upload that is already the secrets directory failed
findings.detail: Uploading environment files straight into the secrets directory and then recording them made cp copy each file onto itself, which is an error. The files were already exactly where they belonged.
findings.fix: The install step compares resolved paths and, when they are the same directory, records the files without copying.

findings.title: A full-table read exceeded the CLI's default request deadline
findings.detail: A repository sync failed with network_timeout after 30 seconds. The read was slow, not broken, but the caller could not tell those apart.
findings.fix: The row helper sets a 90 second request deadline on every tool call.

findings.title: The development runtime gives an app its own empty copies of its databases
findings.detail: Declaring databases in notis.config.ts makes the hidden workspaces-dev runtime app materialise its own repositories and workspaces databases, separate from the installed app's. Two consequences. Slug lookup from outside the app runtime became ambiguous, which is how the skills address databases, and it started failing with 'Several databases use the slug repositories'. And the app mounted under Local development reads the dev app's copies, which are empty, so it shows first-run onboarding rather than the real rows a skill just wrote.
findings.fix: The row helper resolves by listing databases and choosing the one owned by the installed app, preferring the copy that holds rows, so a stale empty twin can never win. The app showing real data in the portal still needs a deploy: that is what binds the bundle to the installed app and its databases.

findings.title: apps verify --mode live reported success on a route that failed to load
findings.detail: Live verify passed both routes. A screenshot of the same live run shows 'Could not load workspaces -- Runtime request failed: Route not found'. Verify's criterion is that nothing throws during render, and a well-behaved error state satisfies that, so an app that handles failure gracefully is indistinguishable from one that works. The underlying error is expected: the app has never been deployed, so the manifest carries no routes and runtime_query cannot resolve one.
findings.fix: Not fixed. Recorded in the wishlist: live verify should assert that declared databases actually returned data, otherwise it grades error handling rather than the app.

findings.title: The skill told the user to send env files through chat, which publishes them
findings.detail: The repository skill originally said to ask the user to send the repository's env files as an upload. A file attached to a conversation goes through FileHandler.upload_to_supabase, which writes to the 'attachments' bucket -- public -- and returns a permanent unsigned public URL. Following that instruction with a production .env would have published every key in it. It was never executed: the files in this run were written straight into the secrets directory, so nothing reached storage.
findings.fix: The skill now forbids routing an env file through a chat attachment or any tool that mints a durable URL, and instead has the user place the files directly in the secrets directory. secrets-install accepts that directory as its own source.

findings.title: An app can now write a file into the cloud computer, and only write
findings.detail: upload_sandbox_file insisted on an http URL, which meant any file had to be published before it could be delivered. Views were also barred from every sandbox tool, so an app could not deliver one at all. Both were reasonable defaults and together they left credentials with no safe route.
findings.fix: The tool accepts content as base64 or utf-8 alongside url, plus an optional mode. VIEW_FORBIDDEN_TOOL_NAMES subtracts this one name, and the shell-mode gate gains a portal-view door that only the upload path opens. Proven against the running server: upload returns 200 with a matching sha256 and the file lands at 0600, while list and download both return 403.

findings.title: A project's own dev script hijacked our CLI calls
findings.detail: Step 7 runs the repository's dev script to prove it works. The notis repo writes .context/notis-routing.json, a worktree CLI lease, so every later Notis CLI call made from inside that checkout failed with dev_runtime_unavailable. The skill caused this itself and it recurs for any project shipping similar tooling.
findings.fix: The row helper runs the CLI from /vercel/sandbox, outside any checkout, so a lease belonging to the project under test can never capture our calls. The skill also warns about it for hand-run commands.

findings.title: Workspace creation fell back to a branch called main
findings.detail: With no repository row, workspace.sh defaulted the base to 'main' and failed with 'fatal: invalid reference: origin/main' on a repository whose default is beta. The error reads like a git problem rather than a missing row.
findings.fix: The base is resolved from git (symbolic-ref refs/remotes/origin/HEAD) when the row has none, so the fallback is the repository's real default.

findings.title: A hand-rolled gh pr create left the app blind
findings.detail: The agent opened a real pull request with gh directly instead of workspace.sh pr, so nothing synced and the row kept reporting no pull request while #1873 was open. It then tried to repair the row by hand rather than syncing.
findings.fix: The skill now says to use workspace.sh pr rather than gh, and that sync is the repair tool for a stale row.

findings.title: Republishing the skills forked duplicates
findings.detail: publish-skills.sh always called CREATE_SKILL, so each run made a second skill with the same name. Both then materialised in the sandbox and an agent would read whichever copy it found first.
findings.fix: The script looks the skill up by name and updates in place, creating only when none exists. The two duplicates it made were deleted.

findings.title: Editing the tree while a live test ran killed four turns
findings.detail: The dev stack runs with --reload-backend. Saving a server file mid-run reloaded the backend and killed the in-flight conversation turn; four interactions died that way and one inbound message was dropped before it became an interaction. The repo's own guidance says to sequence edits into quiet windows, and this run did not.
findings.fix: Not a code fix. Either stop editing while a live conversation test is running, or run the validation against a stack started without --reload-backend.

findings.title: The per-surface shell re-cut turned the app from a board into a product
findings.detail: run_sandbox_shell is now exposed to views and run_desktop_shell is text-only, which is the right split: a desktop shell reachable from a third-party bundle would be a pivot onto the user's own machine. Before this the app could only display rows a skill had written.
findings.fix: The app declares run_sandbox_shell and drives the skills' own scripts. GitHub sign-in is a real control that reads gh auth status, starts the device flow and shows the code; every repository and workspace has a Sync that runs the same sync a skill runs. There is no second implementation to drift.

findings.title: A caller cannot override an injected session variable
findings.detail: run_sandbox_shell accepts an env argument, but the executor merges it as {**command_env, **sandbox_env}, so the session environment wins. That precedence is correct -- otherwise an app could replace NOTIS_JWT and act as someone else -- but the argument silently does nothing for any variable the session already sets, NOTIS_API_BASE among them.
findings.fix: Not a code change. Documented in the wishlist so nobody spends an afternoon on it. It is also why an app-driven sync cannot be exercised against a local dev backend: the sandbox is handed localhost:3001 and no caller can point it elsewhere.

wishes.title: Row-write tool names are content hashes
wishes.cost: Creating a database returns a write tool named LOCAL_NOTIS_DATABASE_UPSERT_REPOSITO_3AD526820B9519B6E71F. The slug is truncated and a twenty-character hash is appended, so the name cannot be predicted from the slug, cannot be written into notis.config.ts before the database exists, and cannot be hard-coded in a skill that is meant to work for any installer of the app.
wishes.want: A stable, derivable write tool name per database slug, or a generic write tool that takes the slug as an argument the way LOCAL_NOTIS_DATABASE_QUERY already does.

wishes.title: An app cannot start work, only display it
wishes.cost: Everything this product actually does is a shell action on the cloud computer: clone, worktree, setup, push, open a pull request. An app is a React bundle whose only outward call is a declared tool, so the buttons that would make this a product cannot exist. The user has to go to a chat surface and ask, then come back to the app to see the result.
wishes.want: A way for an app to hand work to an agent: a hook that starts a skill or an agent task with arguments and returns a handle the UI can follow to completion.

wishes.title: No change feed, so state has to be polled
wishes.cost: Workspace state moves while nobody is looking at the app: a setup finishes, checks go green, a pull request merges. The runtime bridge is request/response over fetch, so the only options are a manual refresh or an interval that spends tool calls on rows that mostly have not changed.
wishes.want: A subscription hook over an app-owned database, so a row written by a skill on the sandbox reaches an open app view without polling.

wishes.title: No secret-shaped property
wishes.cost: A repository's environment files are the most sensitive thing this app touches. There is no property type that means 'this exists and is valid but must never be rendered or returned in full', so the schema stores a status and a file list and deliberately keeps the values out of the database entirely.
wishes.want: A secret property type that stores a reference plus metadata, is redacted in every query response by default, and can be resolved only by a shell action running as that user.

wishes.title: An app cannot see the cloud computer
wishes.cost: The first onboarding step is signing the GitHub CLI in, and the app has no way to ask whether that already happened. Nothing writes it to a database and an app cannot run a command to check.
wishes.want: A read-only capability for a few cloud computer facts behind the same install-time prompt that workspaceDatabases: 'read' already uses.

wishes.title: Declared skills should be able to point at a directory
wishes.cost: An app can declare a skill from its own source tree, but only as one markdown file, so a skill with scripts has to be published out of band and attached by id. The app source stops being the complete source of the product.
wishes.want: Accept a directory path in skills[].path and package it during apps build the way the source snapshot is already packaged.

wishes.title: A permanent failure should not be described as retryable
wishes.cost: The 503 on every row write said 'Retry after tool discovery recovers.' Nothing was recovering: generated tools have no provider file-upload schema, so the condition was permanent. That wording sent the first debugging pass toward a transient-outage theory before the real cause showed up.
wishes.want: Distinguish 'this schema is temporarily unresolvable' from 'this tool has no such schema'. Only the first is a retry.

wishes.title: Document what the sandbox image does not have
wishes.cost: Three separate stops came from image assumptions: Python is 3.9 not 3.12, /dev/fd does not exist so process substitution fails, and the GitHub CLI is installed but signed out. Each was only discoverable by running into it.
wishes.want: A short, maintained note on the sandbox baseline: interpreter versions, shell features that are absent, which CLIs ship and what state they ship in.

wishes.title: Live verify should distinguish a working route from a graceful failure
wishes.cost: Live verify passed two routes that were both rendering an error state. Building an app that fails politely is good practice and it made the check meaningless, so the failure was only caught by looking at a screenshot.
wishes.want: In live mode, assert that each declared database returned at least one successful response, and fail the route when every runtime call errored.

wishes.title: Local development should be able to read the installed app's data
wishes.cost: The development runtime materialises its own empty databases, so the app under Local development shows first-run onboarding while the installed app holds the real rows. Iterating on a view of live data means deploying, which is exactly the step the workflow says to avoid until the user has tested locally.
wishes.want: An opt-in that points a dev session at the installed app's databases, so local iteration can be done against real data without deploying.

wishes.title: There was no safe way to hand a credential file to the cloud computer (built)
wishes.cost: Every agent-driven route from a user's machine to the sandbox goes through a durable URL in the public attachments bucket. For a screenshot that is fine. For a .env it means publishing production keys at a permanent address, so the only correct advice is that the agent must not carry the file at all -- which leaves the user doing it by hand.
wishes.want: Built. upload_sandbox_file now accepts inline content and an optional mode, and views may call that one tool. The Repositories view sends environment files straight from the browser to the sandbox at 0600, with no URL and nothing stored.

wishes.title: A job primitive to go with shell access
wishes.cost: A shell call is one request/response, so anything genuinely long -- a clone, a dependency install, a test run -- has to be started detached and polled. Every app that touches the cloud computer will now reimplement that.
wishes.want: start, status, tail and wait in the SDK. It is the same shape as the job.sh this app's skills already ship.

timeline.event: Dev stack up for the target user; local backend drives the real sandbox.
Sandbox baseline probed: gh signed out, Python 3.9, root sudo available, an existing notis clone on beta with no secrets.
Conductor app registered and both app-owned databases created.
Both skills published with their script bundles and attached to the app.
App builds and both routes verify clean against fixture data.
Skill bundles confirmed materialising in the sandbox through the real sync path.
Found and fixed the absolute-path write bug; 81 CLI handler tests pass including the fail-closed guarantee.
Sandbox routed at the patched backend through a temporary tunnel; row writes with absolute paths succeed from the sandbox.
Full pipeline proven on a public repository: clone, register, discover, secrets, worktree, sync. Tree reports clean with secrets in place.
GitHub device grant expired unapproved; private-repository steps still blocked on that one approval.
GitHub device grant approved as mindtheflo; git identity set from the account.
Private clone of mindtheflo/notis succeeded; setup.sh, dev.sh and archive.sh discovered; python3.12 installed as a prerequisite.
Repository setup finished detached; environment files staged outside every checkout.
Workspace created off beta, change committed with env files provably excluded, pull request #1869 opened.
Full server suite ran inside the workspace: 6301 passed, 13 failed, 4 minutes.
Failures attributed: 12 are sandbox-environment dependent, 1 fails identically on origin/beta. None caused by this branch.
Demo repository and its workspace removed; the app now holds only the real notis repository and its open pull request.
Sandbox reset to a pre-onboarding state; gh left signed in as mindtheflo.
App deployed to the account; the live portal render shows the real from-scratch onboarding state.
Inline upload shipped and proven end to end; 72 tests pass across the two affected suites.
Conversation-driven validation finished: repository set up, workspace created, pull request #1873 opened. Four skill defects found and fixed.
Shell tools re-cut per surface; app rebuilt around real cloud computer access. GitHub sign-in and per-row sync are now controls, not copyable prompts.
